thread_analysis.thread_summary: An internal Allion (Itsuo Sakai, Toshitaka Mochizuki, Jun Wang, Kenichi Ushiroebisu) engineering thread for the Alps Alpine HM26 project, spanning January 31 - February 4, 2025, documents a multi-day, multi-stage troubleshooting effort to get a Qualcomm WCN685x-based device into RF PHY Direct Test Mode (DTM) for InterLab automated tester connection, plus a brief administrative note about missing Japan/Taiwan RF PHY test plan files.
all_questions_found: How is a Qualcomm WCN685x-based device put into RF PHY DTM mode for InterLab automated tester testing, when the standard QDART Android platform guide doesn't document this, and what tool-launch, configuration, cabling, and DUT-connection obstacles must be resolved along the way? (see thread_0033_case_01)

(Administrative, not separately cased) Confirming and resending the correct RF PHY Test Plan files (filenames ending in (AJ) and (AT), covering Japan and Taiwan test sites respectively) after an initial file went missing in transit -- routine document-sharing follow-up without a generalizable technical lesson.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Case_01 documents an unusually granular, real-time internal engineering troubleshooting log rather than a customer-facing Q&A -- valuable precisely because it captures the full layered diagnostic process (tool deployment -> configuration mismatch -> cabling -> DUT availability) for a specific, reusable technical scenario: enabling RF PHY DTM mode on Qualcomm WCN685x-based chipsets for InterLab automated certification testing. Each layer's symptom (tool won't launch, Enable produces an error, etc.) could otherwise be misdiagnosed as a different layer's problem.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0033_case_01 for the full layered decision logic across tool deployment, configuration, cabling, and DUT-connection diagnosis.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See thread_0033_case_01; the primary risk is significant wasted engineering time from misattributing a later-stage symptom (e.g., the Enable error) to an earlier-stage cause (e.g., assuming it's a COM port misconfiguration when the actual cause is an unconnected DUT) without working through the full diagnostic chain.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: No significant consulting-side mistakes identified -- the consultant (Sakai) maintained close, iterative back-and-forth troubleshooting with the on-site engineer across multiple days, refining advice at each new symptom rather than issuing one-shot guidance.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a customer's existing test procedure documentation has a gap (here, RF PHY DTM connection for InterLab automated testing on a specific chipset), check the chipset vendor's own dedicated technical documentation (not just the customer's adapted platform guide) for the missing procedure, and expect that real-world execution of vendor-documented tool/cable procedures may diverge from the documentation in multiple sequential ways (missing dependencies, UI mismatches, cable type ambiguity, and equipment availability conflicts) that each require separate diagnosis rather than assuming a single root cause.
